title: The peace
hookLine: peace be with you, and with your spirit: a handshake, hug or bow

cards: Hand out, then a tiny pause. Is this a handshake person, a hug person, or a nod-from-across-the-aisle person? In the middle of the service everything stops, and strangers turn to greet each other.
A small boy shakes every hand within reach, twice. Two people who snapped at each other in the parking lot meet eyes and have to decide something. A woman in the front bows with her palms together.
And the same words go back and forth across the pews: "Peace be with you." "And with your spirit."

teach.b: It looks like a social break. In the rite it's more: the church making peace with itself before it goes further. Four roots.

teach.h: A LOCKED ROOM: PEACE BE UNTO YOU.
teach.b: First, a locked room, the one from day six hundred fifty-two. On the evening of the resurrection, in John's Gospel, the disciples hide behind shut doors, afraid.
Jesus stands among them, and his first words are no complaint: "Peace be unto you." A couple of verses later, he says it again. Christians who pass the peace pass on his greeting.

teach.h: AN HOLY KISS, AND ONE MIND.
teach.b: Near the end of Romans, Paul writes a line that would startle some congregations now: "Salute one another with an holy kiss." Some churches still call this the kiss of peace.
In the Orthodox liturgy it comes just before the creed, with a call to love one another so the church can confess its faith with one mind. Third, the gift.

teach.h: FIRST BE RECONCILED, THEN THE GIFT.
teach.b: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus says that if you bring your gift to the altar and remember someone has something against you, "Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift."

Some churches place the peace just before the gifts come forward, with that verse in mind. In the Catholic Mass the sign of peace comes later, just before communion. Same gesture, a different place, a meaning in each.
Fourth, the hands. A handshake in one country, a bow in another, a hug where everyone knows everyone. The form bends.

how: In Catholic, Orthodox, Anglican, Lutheran, Methodist and some other churches, the congregation exchanges a sign of peace during the service with a handshake, embrace or bow, saying "peace be with you"; where it falls in the service differs from church to church.

o: a pause for silent prayer after the sermon
a closing hymn asking God for world peace
a greeting of peace passed around during worship

p: salute one another with an holy kiss

s: the peace is only a friendly intermission
it's the church making peace with itself, passing on the risen Jesus's own greeting.
in John's Gospel, Jesus says "peace be unto you" more than once that evening
he says it when he first stands among them, and again a couple of verses later.
in the Orthodox liturgy, the kiss of peace comes just before the creed
with a call to love one another, so the church can confess its faith with one mind. the Catholic Mass places it just before communion.

games.q: you've brought your gift to the altar. standing there, you remember that someone has something against you. what does Jesus say to do?
o: offer the gift now, and sort it out afterward.
leave the gift there, go and be reconciled, then come back.
offer the gift and say a prayer for them.
games.why: "leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother." the gift can wait; the relationship can't.

practice: Bring one person to mind, someone you love or someone you're at odds with, the parking-lot person in your life, and hold their face a moment without arguing with it. Then, silently, wish them peace.
If you pray, say the risen Jesus's words over them, peace be unto you; if you don't, simply wish them well and mean it, even a little.

wordCard.voice: The peace. The moment in a service when people greet one another with Jesus's words, peace be with you, before going on together.

orig.note: Greek: peace, the word in Jesus's greeting to the disciples in John 20:19.

carryVoice: Your line: peace be with you. And with your spirit. Rest well.
